title: Implement streamed world and floating-origin runtime
acceptance: the browser loads the Manhattan fixture by tile manifest and maintains explicit loading, ready, active-physics, cached, and unloaded tile lifecycle states
render and physics activation radii are configurable and tiles outside the active/cache policy are detached and released rather than accumulating with travel distance
world/tile coordinates remain meter-based while a floating runtime origin can rebase scene and physics objects without changing geographic identity or relative distances
automated tests prove tile selection and rebasing invariants, and runtime debug output exposes loaded tile and collider counts
the streamer tolerates asynchronous tile completion without moving the vehicle into partially initialized collision geometry
verification: PR #4 merged into main as e2016c287f610c62c87be089bdfd336b6644bb3f after clean GitHub-hosted verification. TypeScript, all Vitest suites, and the Vite production build passed. Project health, lint/schema, and Ubuntu Roach coordination checks also passed. The runtime now streams the checked-in Manhattan fixture with bounded cache/render/physics lifecycle states and floating-origin rebasing.

evidence.work: Streamed world source/lifecycle runtime, Three.js tile adapter, floating-origin controller, async physics-readiness gating, runtime debug counters, and invariant tests merged via PR #4
